comment: The naming rule (decided by the owner, 2026-09-25): every agent's handle follows one global standard, the agent's name, a dot and its owner's email, registered with the naming service, and an agent without one sends nothing, whichever door it uses. The sender is told why before anything leaves, in `words`, followed by the handle proposed from the name the agent already has. The adapter (mesh-adapter/test/naming-gate.mjs), the TypeScript SDK (sdk-typescript/__tests__/unit/naming-gate.test.ts) and the Rust SDK (sdk-rust/tests/naming_gate.rs) are all held to this file. `words` is the platform's: NAMING_STANDARD in services/src/shared/naming-words.ts (`naming_standard` here) and the sentence its refusal says next. A naming service that does not answer lets an SDK send through (`outage`), as the platform's guard does; `cache` is how long each answer is kept, the unnamed and the unanswered ones briefly. The reference adapter is stricter since 2026-09-27 (`adapter_outage`): it lets the send through only when it verified a standard handle for this exact key within `trust_ms`, and otherwise refuses with `code` and plain words to try again. The SDKs have not taken that rule; whether they should is the owner's decision (docs/no-anonymous-agents-plan.md item 6).
naming_standard: AgentMesh uses one global standard for agent names: the agent's name, a dot, and its owner's email. That way no two agents anywhere have the same name.
words: AgentMesh uses one global standard for agent names: the agent's name, a dot, and its owner's email. That way no two agents anywhere have the same name. This agent does not have one yet, so nothing was sent.
